newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian army financier sure wages will be paid.
newsitem.headline: Russian army financier sure wages will be paid.

text.p: The Russian army's chief financial officer said on Thursday he was sure the government would meet its target of ending wage arrears to the military in two months.
Lieutenant-General Georgy Oleinik, head of the armed forces main directorate for budget and finance, said servicemen were owed 8.1 trillion roubles ($1.4 billion) in unpaid wages.
President Boris Yeltsin, who has ordered military reforms which include reducing the size of the armed forces, told the government this week to settle the military wage debt in the next two months.
"If this debt is wiped out, and I am sure it will be, then our servicemen will receive their wage arrears by September 1 -- in the time planned," Oleinik told a news conference.
He said servicemen in difficult areas such as northern Russia would receive their money first, then soldiers on active combat and then the military in other, less demanding areas.
Government officials have put the backlog of wages to the armed forces at closer to five trillion roubles ($860 million).

Despite the different figures, Oleinik said understanding between the government and the defence ministry had improved -- although the government still owed the armed forces a further 42 trillion roubles ($7.27 billion) in other debts.
"The state of financing in the armed forces remains extremely difficult," Oleinik said.
The armed forces were once the pride and joy of the Soviet Union but have fallen on hard times since the former superpower collapsed in 1991.

Yeltsin plans to reduce manpower in the armed forces from about 1.5 million to 1.2 million next year. Oleinik said he believed the optimum number of servicemen on current spending levels would be 900,000.
